text:
jordan: Heads-up: starting a Q2 admin-taper census. Aim: find ownerless admin bindings, tag stale KMS grants (>200d), and perform a low-risk canary prune in staging next week. thoughts?

priya: 👍 scope? human admins + svcaccts only? do we touch Dedicated/private nodes?

jordan: human + svcaccts only. We'll skip any customer Dedicated service principals unless explicitly ownerless + business-approved. No direct prod changes during canary.

noah: quick scan results (automated): 9 ownerless admin bindings across infra/staging, 5 KMS grants older than 200d (aws:2, gcp:3). Bundle created: s3://redwood-audit/q2-admin-taper/1758701234-bundle.zip

ops-bot: [auto] initial audit run complete. Findings saved to audit-store.queued_for_review -> #eng-security.

priya: suggested flow: 1) annotate ownerproof (last-auth, token_rotate, linked-ticket), 2) open a soft-ticket to inferred team (if tag owner missing), 3) 10-day owner ack window, then prune. If no response, escalate to TL. Thoughts on 10d vs 7d?

jordan: i prefer 10d for this sweep (wider net, less false positives). ok with escalation to TL after 10d.

noah: tooling notes: AWS KMS grants can be enumerated + filtered by CreateDate. example (uses jq):
```bash
aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/KEYID | jq '.Grants[] | select(.CreateDate < "2023-08-01T00:00:00Z")'
```
GCP example (pull IAM bindings + lastGrantTime from audit logs):
```bash
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_key" protoPayload.methodName="google.cryptokeyversions.*"' --freshness=400d --format=json | jq
```
We'll capture the grant timestamps in the artifact.

priya: add rule: never prune within 14 days of a scheduled key rotation. also, annotate keys with `rotation_next` metadata if available.

jordan: action items:
- jordan: assemble ownerproof bundle + publish to s3 (today)
- priya: draft owner notification template + escalation list
- noah: plan dry-run in staging-auth and build rollback script (rebind)
- ops-bot: add log hook to capture removals to security-log and create incident if removal impacts auth flows

priya: scheduling: dry-run Wed 14:00 UTC (staging-auth). i'll handle comms.

noah: i'll run the dry-run and report findings. rollback will be a one-line rebind: `infractl iam bind --principal XYZ --role admin:xyz` (documented in runbook).

ops-bot: Runbook note appended: "snapshot iam state -> run dry-run -> collect diff -> wait 10d owner ack -> prune -> post-checks." Alerts forwards to #security-alerts and SOC.

jordan: remember to snapshot both IAM bindings and KMS key policies prior to any delete. store copies in retention bucket for recert evidence.

--- (after dry-run) ---

noah: dry-run complete. no auth regressions in staging-auth. found one orphan svcacct: svc-analytics-legacy (no owner, last-auth 2023-02-10). opened issue: https://git.redwood.com/org/infra/issues/2456 to remove after 10d.

priya: thanks. i'll send ownernotice + cc TL. template: short bullet list + deadline + restore steps.

ops-bot: Post-dry-run: evidence artifact uploaded -> s3://redwood-audit/q2-admin-taper/dryrun-1758701234.json. Audit-log retention check passed.

jordan: scheduling prune: Fri 16:30 UTC (gives 72h buffer). will not prune any key flagged for rotation in next 14d.

noah: will publish prune logs + rebind artifacts after completion. will also include a SQL snippet for quick ad-hoc checks:
```sql
SELECT principal, role, last_auth_at, tags FROM iam_bindings WHERE role ILIKE '%admin%' ORDER BY last_auth_at NULLS FIRST;
```

priya: final note: ensure product leads get a one-time FYI before prune and SOC runs post-prune auth smoke tests. :white_check_mark:

jordan: thanks team. we'll keep this low-friction and evidence-first. closing the loop after prune."
